end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The pack is removed from a vehicle by a party qualified to work on a 400 volt system, with the vehicle's high-voltage system isolated by the vehicle first.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. No party has agreed it and nothing enforces it.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The service documentation states the assumption at the point of removal, not in a decommissioning record the removing party never sees.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A person works on an energised pack. This is the assumption whose failure is fatal rather than merely inconvenient, which is why it is first and why no control in this item can be relied upon to catch it.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: At removal the pack may be energised and within its operating envelope, and its state cannot be determined from the item after removal.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Derived from the chemistry: a lithium-ion cell retains a hazardous voltage long after load is removed. The item cannot measure its own state once disconnected.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The final state record states that it describes the item's state at removal and is not a statement about the pack's charge.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A removed pack is treated as safe because the item recorded a normal state before removal, and is handled accordingly while still holding a hazardous charge.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The receiving party can reach a measurement of the removed pack's voltage before it does anything else.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. It depends on the receiving party's equipment and training, neither of which this project controls.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The receiver assumption record passed with the service documentation. The control is communication, not enforcement, and it is recorded as such.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: The receiving party acts before measuring. Nothing in the item prevents this and nothing in this corpus addresses it.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The cell chemistry's own end-of-life requirements are met by the cell supplier and are not the item's to discharge.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared and consistent with the item definition's scope statement, which places thermal runaway and cell chemistry outside the item's boundary.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The scope statement in FB2-SAF-ITE-000001 classifies the hazard as inherent to the chemistry rather than to the item, so the boundary decision is visible and can be challenged.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A cell is treated as a component rather than as a hazardous material at end of life, and the item's boundary was wrong in a way that matters at exactly one moment in the product's life.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The item is not modified after removal in a way that a removing party would reasonably expect to be safe.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. Not enforceable by the item.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: None. This record states the assumption and states that no control exists, which is the honest position and is the reason the assumption appears here at all.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: The item is opened or its contacts bridged, and a stored charge discharges through an unintended path.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
